clue.text: Later a beer was disturbed by a gossip-monger

indicators.note: letters that were disturbed have been stirred up, so these three words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Someone spreading rumours knocks over a pint of lager later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was disturbed' rearranges the ten letters of LATER A BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A talebearer carries tales about others, which is exactly what a rumour-spreading gossip does.

clue.text: A method used elsewhere

parts.note: a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A technique imported from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is away is absent, somewhere other than here.

clue.text: Show clearly that church is in support of English and French wine

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so the church letters go below the others

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman proves he backs both English and French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a quality is to display or reveal it plainly.

clue.text: Jaguar, for example, emits this engine noise

explanation.surface: A sports car makes this sound when started.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaguar works twice: the big cat gives a roar, and the car's engine roars too.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cat's deep cry and the loud sound of a revving motor are both called a roar.

clue.text: Bank, say, on dollar to get a reddish-brown jumper

indicators.note: say signals that the next piece is only how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a bank of seats or keys is a row, and row is pronounced like roe
buck is slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A banker bets money on a fox-coloured athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is a male roe deer, a reddish-brown animal that leaps nimbly.

clue.text: But is one thrown in picture da's making?

definitions.text: But is one thrown in picture da's making?

indicators.note: the making of these letters means they are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: In a slapstick film by Dad, isn't something always thrown?
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges PICTUREDAS; the whole clue also describes slapstick comedy, where this is the missile of choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick films famously feature a creamy dessert hurled into someone's face.

clue.text: Diamond-shaped piece of glass, the French, by right, make for one in a row

parts.note: a quarrel is a small diamond-shaped pane, as in a leaded window
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A glazier fits a diamond pane with French help for someone in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow here: a person in a row is having an argument, not standing in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone involved in a heated argument or dispute is a quarreller.

clue.text: Leader of guys, in the first half, at rugby

indicators.note: only the opening half of the word guys is used, its first two letters

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: The captain led the lads well in the first half of the rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a spiritual teacher or guide whom followers look to for direction.

clue.text: Maigret sat out, like one on the bench

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and reassembled

explanation.surface: Simenon's detective sat out, as though he were a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MAIGRET SAT; Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional French detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a lay or junior judge who sits on the bench in a lower court.

clue.text: Half of them take the pulse

indicators.note: half of the word them means just its first two letters

parts.note: to rob is to take by theft

explanation.surface: Half the patients have their heart rate measured.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, such as a heartbeat.

clue.text: Gambler cured?

explanation.surface: Has the punter been cured of his habit?
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler is one who bets; someone cured of an illness is said to be better again.

clue.text: You'll announce record that brings Christmas cheer

indicators.note: to announce is to speak aloud, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: you'll said aloud sounds like yule, an old word for Christmas
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A promise that a recording will spread festive joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A yule log, the large log burnt at Christmas or the chocolate cake, is a festive source of seasonal good cheer.

clue.text: Metropolitan police chief who marshals his forces?

definitions.text: Metropolitan police chief who marshals his forces?

parts.words: Metropolitan police chief who marshals his forces?
parts.note: Scotland Yard is the London Metropolitan Police headquarters, so its master would run it; but really this is the railway official who marshals trains in a goods yard

explanation.surface: London's top policeman deploys his officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, a common name for London's Metropolitan Police, suggests a police boss; the 'forces' are really wagons shunted in a rail yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardmaster supervises a railway yard, directing the shunting and assembling of trains.

clue.text: Titled woman on ship with imitation cuckoo-flower

parts.note: Lady is the title of a peeress or knight's wife
SS stands for steamship
mock means fake or imitation

explanation.surface: An aristocrat on a liner is carrying a fake cuckoo-flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo-flower is another common name for Cardamine pratensis, a pale lilac meadow plant.

clue.text: Theatre-in-the-round

parts.note: a staging term that here points to Shakespeare's famous round London playhouse, and also to a sphere

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's playhouse on the South Bank was circular, and a sphere is itself round.

clue.text: Singular nerve, going without a whip!

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: going without the letter a means it is taken out

parts.note: nerve means courage

explanation.surface: It takes rare nerve to go without the lash!
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a lash used for flogging, so a whip.

clue.text: A bit of a row

explanation.surface: Part of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a small fragment, and also a fight or quarrel.

clue.text: Gloomy bar

explanation.surface: A depressing pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Black means dismal or bleak; to black something is to ban or boycott it, as unions once blacked goods.

clue.text: Travel free at rear of carriage

parts.note: to rid is to free from something

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fare-dodger sits at the back of the train.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to journey on horseback or in a vehicle.

clue.text: Jewel carried by episcopalians

indicators.note: letters carried by a word are held within it, so look for a run inside episcopalians

explanation.surface: Bishops' church members wear a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone.

clue.text: A thick piece of wood across width of ship

parts.note: a beam is a long sturdy timber

explanation.surface: A heavy timber is laid across the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term meaning at right angles to the vessel's length, level with its middle.

clue.text: Greed of a vicar, perhaps, going to Spain

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: E is Spain's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A clergyman's covetousness might take him to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme desire for wealth, a synonym for greed.

clue.text: Big traffic congestion backing-up to Oregon

indicators.note: in a down clue backing up means the word is read upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: a traffic jam is congestion on the road
OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon

explanation.surface: Huge tailbacks stretch as far as Oregon.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means large or important.

clue.text: Letter from girl I have contracted to follow

indicators.note: the second piece is set to come after the first in the answer

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
I have contracted is the short form I've

explanation.surface: A note from a young woman to say she has caught something.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a written message, especially a long or formal one.

clue.text: Fake jewels take half an hour for a scientist

parts.note: paste is glass used to make imitation gems

indicators.note: only the latter half of the word hour is used, its last two letters

explanation.surface: Costume jewellery takes thirty minutes for a lab researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist behind pasteurisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was a celebrated nineteenth-century French microbiologist.

clue.text: The endless wild party?

indicators.note: endless means the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: rash means reckless or wild

explanation.surface: A wild party with no end.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal slang for a lively celebration or bash.

clue.text: Amount taken to the sea in France in a warm spell

parts.note: a sum is an amount
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A sum of money is spent at the French seaside during a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is the hottest season of the year.

clue.text: A field of granular snow, smooth on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: even means level or smooth

explanation.surface: Climbers cross a smooth snowfield on their ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns EVEN into NEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Névé is young granular snow that has partly melted and refrozen, at the top of a glacier.

clue.text: Announced rain-check?

indicators.note: something announced is said aloud, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: rain said aloud sounds the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A postponement is declared because of bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or hold back.

clue.text: Reinforced vessel, useful at parties

explanation.surface: A strong boat that livens up a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship strengthened to cut through polar ice; also a game or remark that relaxes strangers at a gathering.

clue.text: He comes back, carrying bill per person

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other piece inside
comes back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
AC is short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: He returns, bringing the bill for every diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns HE into EH; 'carrying' puts AC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Each means individually, for every one of a group.

clue.text: Eight nervy characters out for a great deal

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and reassembled

explanation.surface: Eight jittery types go out on the town in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EIGHT NERVY; 'characters' just says it is letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything is all there is, loosely a huge amount.
